name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Per-friend sharing controls, and two real bugs found while building them.

Added per-friend library sharing: pick which of this server's own libraries a specific friend can see, defaulting to everything (unchanged from before). Enforced through Jellyfin's own EnabledFolders account policy rather than anything this plugin polices itself - the same mechanism used to restrict a family member's login. The admin picks an existing local Jellyfin user for this rather than the plugin creating one automatically: IUserManager.CreateUserAsync does not work reliably on every server build - it can leave a new user's AuthenticationProviderId unset and then fail its own save with a NOT NULL constraint, before ever handing the created user back to plugin code to fix up, since the failure happens inside Jellyfin's own creation path. Reusing an account Jellyfin's admin UI already created successfully sidesteps the bug entirely, and is arguably better anyway - the account is fully visible and manageable from the normal Dashboard, not a hidden one this plugin invents. Also found and fixed: listing local Jellyfin users threw MissingMethodException on at least one real server build, because the member exposing it changed shape (a `Users` property in the NuGet package this plugin compiles against, a `GetUsers()` method on the actual running server) - now read through reflection so it works against either shape instead of binding to whichever one happened to be present at compile time.

Pools got two fixes. First, adding a friend you already have to a pool used to fail outright ("already friends") because it went through the same handshake used for a genuinely new contact - defeating the entire point of a pool, which is not repeating that handshake for people you're already connected to. Adding an existing friend now just adds them to the pool locally and sends them a notice, no accept step needed since the two servers already trust each other; only a real stranger goes through the full friend-request flow. Second, the notice this sends (and the sharing-update notice from the paragraph above) was never actually being received on the other end - the request carried no API key, so the friend's server would have rejected it outright as unauthorized. Neither had ever been exercised against a live peer before now, so this had gone unnoticed. Multiple pools already worked correctly; nothing was blocking that.

Also fixed a CSS bug in last release's own black-text fix: it forced light text using an ID selector, which outranks Jellyfin's own button/element styling by CSS specificity and could make some things - like a light-background button expecting dark text - illegible in the other direction. Rewritten with :where() so it only fills in a color where nothing else set one, and never overrides an element's own deliberate styling.

160 tests (up from 150), including coverage for the existing-friend pool fast path, the pool notice fan-out, and the sharing feature's rejection paths.
